text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- A report that Premier Gyula Horn had nominated journalist Tibor Thurzo for the post of vice president of Hungarian Television drew amazed responses from MTV president Istvan Petak and Free Democrat media expert Peter Molnar yesterday, who both pointed out that the media law does not allow the government to interfere in the selection of MTV executives.
- In an apparent turnabout, Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky speaking to the Austrian daily Die Presse yesterday expressed reservations about a speedy eastward expansion of the European Union.
- Trading on the Stock Exchange yesterday resumed at a hectic pace following a one-week hiatus, bringing the BUX Index to its eighth consecutive record closing at 4,124.81 points, a rise of 22.34.
- The Finance Ministry confirmed yesterday that the Hungarian state has indeed bought back Polgari Bank from GE Capital for the bank's book value.
- After the HUF 8.52 million consolidated loss last year, Corvinbank may be out of the red in 1996, said president and CEO Gyula Pazmandi.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Parliament passed 132 bills and amendments in 1996 as well as 120 parliamentary resolutions, practically duplicating its performance of the previous year.
- The price of telephone calls made through the national telephone company Matav will go up from January 1.
- Postal fees are to increase 18-20 percent, beginning January 1.
- An exhaust analyst instrument that can check the exhaust emission of more than 500 cars per hour without disrupting traffic will make its European debut in Budapest next month.
NEPSZABADSAG

- A survey shows that 41 percent of Hungarians consider the performance of the Horn administration to be neither better nor worse than that of the Antall and Boross governments, while 29 percent consider it to be worse, and 23 percent said it is better.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The surplus of tourism came to $950 million in the first nine months of this year and the total income was $1.883 billion by late October, reports the Ministry of Industry.
- Similarly to the Stock Exchange, the OTC market was also abuzz with activity in 1996.

- The construction of a 10 billion forint state-of-the-art wheel factory is nearing completion in Tatabanya. The plant is built by the US-based Superior Industries International and the German firm Otto Fuchs Metallwerke.

- The consignment warehouse and pawnshop chain BAV expects a pre-tax profit of 402 million forints this year on revenues of 6.2 billion forints . A privatisation strategy for the company is currently being worked out.
- An English-language version of the Hungarian Financial and Stock Exchange Almanac has now been published.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- Total loans of Hungarian commercial banks, graded as "appropriate', increased by 1,000 billion forints between 1993 and 1995, reports the State Banking Supervision.
HAPPY NEW YEAR!
